answer: Charge each voting identity a proof of reserved disk space. Encode the basalt, karst and inlet map archives with an identity-specific salt, commit their roots, then answer unpredictable chunk challenges within a short deadline. One disk cannot cheaply impersonate a thousand full replicas: distinct encodings consume space, while regenerating missing chunks risks missing the deadline. Audit throughout the voting period, not only at entry. Outsourced storage still counts as paid capacity; this limits cheap aliases, not wealthy owners.
